subject: Plan laddering & rollback clauses — credit anchoring question
messages:
From: Sam Cole <sam@cloudpeak.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: aisha.k@cloudpeak.com
Date: 2025-05-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging question: rollback credits and tier laddering

Markus —

Quick question as we're preparing our procurement runbook: CloudPeak may need to step down from the Premier tier to Standard after Q3 if usage growth slows. Procurement is asking for a clear rollback clause and a predictable credit structure tied to deployment tiers rather than ad-hoc credits.

Can Redwood provide a proposal that:
- Defines a laddered credit schedule when customers downgrade within 12 months (e.g., % of committed reserved capacity returned as credits depending on timing)
- Anchors credits to deployment/plan features (burst pools, KV cache retention, prioritized support) so we know which capabilities are rolled back vs retained
- Shows an example with our expected usage (attached) so legal can assess financial impact

We want to avoid one-off credit negotiations at renewal — procurement would prefer a deterministic formula.

Thanks,
Sam
Senior SRE, CloudPeak

Attachments: CloudPeak_Expected_Usage_Q2.csv (CSV, 14KB)

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Sam Cole <sam@cloudpeak.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-14T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question: rollback credits and tier laddering

Sam —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sending expected usage. We can definitely propose a deterministic ladder instead of ad-hoc credits. High level we usually split rollbacks into two buckets: financial credits (monetary offsets against future invoices) and capability-preservation (features that remain active for a short window or require explicit opt-in to retain).

Draft concept: (we'll attach a worked example)
- Time-based credit decay: 100% of prorated reserved capacity credit if downgrade within 30 days of commit; 60% within 31-120 days; 30% within 121-270 days; 0% after 270 days.
- Feature anchoring: map features to plan flags. e.g., Premier includes: dedicated burst pool, 99.9% SLA, priority support, 48hr audit log retention. On downgrade to Standard: SLA remains at 99.5%, burst pool is reduced to best-effort (with a partial credit for unused burst units), audit log retention drops to 30 days unless customer pays an archival fee.
- Escalation carve-outs: security incidents or regulatory holdbacks are excluded from automatic downgrades for 60 days to allow mitigation.

Questions for you so we can tailor:
1) Is CloudPeak looking for credits applied as one-time invoice credit or as monthly recurring offset?
2) What is the latest date procurement will accept for a hard deadline on rollback protections (i.e., 12mo from purchase vs 18mo)?

I've looped in Lauren to run the dollar math and Grace to validate the feature flags mapping. We'll put together a short worksheet and a sample clause we can present to your procurement/legal team.

Would you be available for a 30 minute review at 1:30pm PT today?

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0192

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, Sam Cole <sam@cloudpeak.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-14T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question: rollback credits and tier laddering

Sam —

Thanks — I took a look at the CSV. Quick numeric example to illustrate how the time-decay would work if CloudPeak chooses a monthly recurring offset vs lump-sum credit: (assume $120k annual reserved commitment for Premier)
- Downgrade at 20 days: prorated unused portion ~ 11/12 of committed term => credit gross = $110k. Under our 100% within 30 days rule that would be issued as either a one-time invoice credit or applied over 3 months as offsets (customer preference).
- Downgrade at 90 days: prorated unused portion ~ 9/12 => $90k gross, applying 60% decay => $54k net credit.
- Downgrade at 180 days: prorated unused portion ~ 6/12 => $60k gross, applying 30% decay => $18k net credit.

Notes:
- We recommend one-time credits for clarity (procurement likes clean ledger entries), but some customers prefer monthly offsets to smooth cash flow.
- Feature anchoring: Grace will propose the default mapping, and customers can opt to pay a small premium to retain specific features on downgrade (e.g., $500/month for extended audit logs).

I'll attach a short worksheet with the math and three example scenarios.

Lauren Bishop
Principal Pricing Analyst, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-plan-ladder-v1.xlsx (Excel, 28KB)

From: Sam Cole <sam@cloudpeak.com>

Markus / team —

This is very helpful, thank you. Procurement will prefer one-time invoice credits where possible. Two follow-ups from legal/procurement:
1) They want the language we propose for the SOW/amendment — explicit wording for the decay schedule and a sample table they can insert.
2) They asked if certain features (priority support, audit retention) can be flagged as "non-degradable" for specific regulated teams under an add-on fee. They'd like the fee schedule spelled out in the doc.

Also — do you support a short neutral arbitration clause for disputes about whether a feature was used (i.e., to determine if a partial-capacity credit should be issued)?

If you can circulate a PDF with the clause + worksheet, procurement will share it with legal. Meeting at 1:30pm PT works for Sam and Aisha.

Thanks,
Sam
